gobekli-tepe.d: Hunter-gatherers raise carved stone pillars — the oldest known sanctuary.

first-farming.t: The first farming in the Fertile Crescent
first-farming.d: Einkorn, barley and lentils are domesticated; the Neolithic Revolution begins.

walls-of-jericho.d: A stone wall and tower around one of the first permanent settlements.

catalhoyuk.d: A large Neolithic town of houses without streets — you entered through the roof.

rice-domesticated.t: Rice is domesticated on the Yangtze
rice-domesticated.d: The beginning of rice farming in East Asia.

mehrgarh.d: An early farming village at the foot of the Baluchistan mountains.

farming-reaches-balkans.d: Neolithic villages such as Karanovo and Slatina — the first farmers in Europe.

provadia-salt.d: Salt production at Solnitsata — by the excavators' account the oldest known town in Europe.

copper-smelting-balkans.d: The Ai Bunar mine near Stara Zagora is among the oldest copper mines in the world.
copper-smelting-balkans.w: Metallurgy during the Copper Age in Europe

maize-mexico.d: Teosinte slowly becomes maize — the staple of every Mesoamerican civilization.

varna-gold.d: The oldest worked gold in the world, found in the necropolis near Varna.

the-wheel.d: The first wheels appear almost at once in Mesopotamia, the North Pontic steppe and Central Europe.

horse-domesticated.d: The Botai culture of the Kazakh steppe — the earliest traces of tamed horses.

cuneiform.d: Accounting marks on clay turn into the first writing.

otzi.d: Killed in the Alps; his mummy was found in 1991 with a bow, an axe and a copper blade.

narmer.d: Upper and Lower Egypt become one kingdom — the dynasties begin.

stonehenge.d: Building starts on the circle that will be reshaped for a thousand years.

harappa-mohenjo-daro.d: Planned cities with drains in the Indus valley.

gilgamesh.d: The king of Uruk becomes the hero of the first great work of literature.

great-pyramid.d: Khufu's tomb — the tallest building in the world for nearly 4,000 years.

caral.d: Pyramids and plazas of Norte Chico — the oldest city in the Americas.

sargon-of-akkad.d: Founds the first empire to unite Mesopotamia.

ziggurat-of-ur.d: Ur-Nammu raises a stepped temple to the moon god Nanna.

minoan-palaces.d: Knossos becomes the centre of Europe's first palace civilization.

code-of-hammurabi.d: 282 laws carved on a basalt stele in Babylon.

thera-eruption.d: One of the most powerful eruptions in history buries Akrotiri.

oracle-bones.d: The earliest Chinese writing — inscriptions on bones and shells.

hittites-sack-babylon.d: Mursili I destroys the city and ends Hammurabi's dynasty.

battle-of-megiddo-1457.d: Thutmose III defeats the Canaanite kings — the first battle described in detail.

akhenaten-aten.t: Akhenaten and the cult of Aten
akhenaten-aten.d: The pharaoh imposes the worship of the sun disc and moves the capital to Amarna.

tutankhamun.d: His short reign is famous for the tomb found intact in 1922.

battle-of-kadesh.d: Ramesses II against the Hittites — the largest chariot battle in history.

first-peace-treaty.d: Egypt and the Hittite kingdom sign a treaty whose text survives on both sides.

bronze-age-collapse.d: Sea Peoples, famine and earthquakes; the Hittites, Mycenae and Ugarit fall.

fall-of-troy.d: By tradition the Achaeans take the city after a ten-year siege.

phoenician-alphabet.d: 22 letters for consonants — the ancestor of Greek, Latin and Cyrillic.

zhou-overthrows-shang.d: At the Battle of Muye the Zhou win and claim the Mandate of Heaven.

king-david.d: According to the Bible, David makes Jerusalem the capital of a united kingdom.

chavin-de-huantar.d: A religious centre in the Andes whose style spreads across Peru.

founding-of-carthage.d: Phoenicians from Tyre found a colony that will become a sea power.

first-olympics.d: A footrace at Olympia — the Greeks count their years from it.

founding-of-rome.d: By legend Romulus founds the city on the Palatine Hill.

homer.d: The Iliad and the Odyssey are written down — the start of European literature.

assyria-takes-israel.d: Sargon II deports the ten northern tribes.

library-of-ashurbanipal.d: Thousands of clay tablets gathered in Nineveh — it is how we know Gilgamesh.

emperor-jimmu.d: In Japanese tradition the first emperor founds the dynasty.

fall-of-nineveh.d: Medes and Babylonians destroy the Assyrian capital.

lydian-coins.d: Electrum coins struck at Sardis — money takes a new shape.

babylonian-captivity.d: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem and the First Temple.

buddha.d: Siddhartha Gautama is born at Lumbini; his teaching will travel across Asia.

confucius.d: Born in Lu; his ethics will shape China for two and a half thousand years.

cyrus-enters-babylon.d: Persia swallows Babylonia; the Jews return to Judea.

roman-republic.d: The Romans expel their last king, Tarquin the Proud.

athenian-democracy.d: The reforms of Cleisthenes give power to the popular assembly.

art-of-war.d: Attributed to Sun Tzu — a treatise still read today.

battle-of-marathon.d: The Athenians stop the first Persian invasion of Greece.

thermopylae.d: Leonidas and the three hundred Spartans hold Xerxes' army in the pass.

salamis.d: Themistocles' Greek fleet crushes the Persians in the narrow strait.

odrysian-kingdom.d: Teres I unites the Thracian tribes into the first Thracian state.

parthenon.d: Pericles begins the temple of Athena on the Acropolis.

peloponnesian-war.d: Athens against Sparta — 27 years of war, told by Thucydides.

trial-of-socrates.d: The Athenians sentence the philosopher to death by hemlock.

platos-academy.d: Europe's first school of higher learning — it runs for nearly 900 years.

chaeronea.d: Philip II of Macedon defeats Athens and Thebes and subdues Greece.

battle-of-issus.d: Alexander puts Darius III to flight.

gaugamela.d: Alexander destroys the Persian Empire for good.

founding-of-alexandria.d: A city on the Nile delta that will become the capital of learning.

death-of-alexander.d: He dies in Babylon at 32; his empire splits among his generals.

chandragupta-maurya.d: Founds the first empire to cover almost all of India.

euclid.d: The Elements — the geometry textbook used until the 20th century.

lighthouse-of-alexandria.d: About 100 metres tall — one of the Seven Wonders of the World.

ashoka-after-kalinga.d: Horrified by the bloodshed, the emperor embraces Buddhism and sends it across the world.

first-punic-war.d: Rome and Carthage clash over Sicily.

hannibal-crosses-alps.d: With an army and elephants the Carthaginian invades Italy.

cannae.d: Hannibal encircles and destroys a Roman army — a classic of tactics.

great-wall.d: Qin Shi Huang joins the separate walls against the Xiongnu.

qin-unifies-china.d: The first emperor imposes one script, one set of measures and one law.

terracotta-army.d: Thousands of clay soldiers guard the first emperor's tomb.

han-dynasty.d: Liu Bang founds the dynasty after which the Chinese still call themselves Han.

zama.d: Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal in Africa.

rosetta-stone.d: One decree in three scripts — the key Champollion used to read hieroglyphs.

destruction-of-carthage.d: Rome razes the city; Corinth falls the same year.

zhang-qian.d: The Han envoy reaches Bactria — the beginning of the Silk Road.

spartacus.d: The Thracian gladiator leads the largest slave revolt against Rome.

carrhae.d: The Parthians destroy Crassus's legions in the desert.

alesia.d: Caesar besieges Vercingetorix and completes the conquest of Gaul.

caesar-crosses-rubicon.d: "The die is cast" — the civil war begins.

ides-of-march.d: Senators murder Julius Caesar in Rome.

actium.d: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra; Egypt becomes Roman.

augustus.d: The Senate grants Octavian the title Augustus; the Republic ends.

teutoburg-forest.d: Arminius's Germans destroy three legions; Rome stops at the Rhine.

crucifixion-of-jesus.d: In Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate; his disciples spread the new faith.

thrace-roman-province.d: Emperor Claudius ends the last Thracian kingdom.

vesuvius-pompeii.d: The eruption buries Pompeii and Herculaneum in ash.
vesuvius-pompeii.w: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD

colosseum.d: The Flavian Amphitheatre opens with a hundred days of games.

destruction-of-second-temple.t: The destruction of the Second Temple
destruction-of-second-temple.d: Titus takes Jerusalem after the Jewish revolt.

cai-lun-paper.d: A court official perfects paper made from bark and rags.

trajan-conquers-dacia.d: Rome reaches beyond the Danube; Dacian gold fills the treasury.

roman-empire-greatest-extent.t: The Roman Empire at its greatest extent
roman-empire-greatest-extent.d: When Trajan dies the empire stretches from Britain to Mesopotamia.

hadrians-wall.d: A wall across Britain marking Rome's northern frontier.

ptolemy-almagest.d: The astronomy and geography of antiquity, gathered in Alexandria.

yellow-turban-rebellion.d: A peasant uprising that shakes the Han dynasty.

red-cliffs.d: Liu Bei and Sun Quan stop Cao Cao — the Three Kingdoms begin.

sasanians.d: Ardashir I overthrows the Parthians and founds a new Persian empire.

teotihuacan-height.d: Over a hundred thousand people live around the Pyramid of the Sun.

battle-of-abritus.d: Goths kill Emperor Decius near modern Razgrad — the first emperor to fall to barbarians.

gupta-empire.d: Chandragupta I opens India's golden age — zero, chess, Kalidasa.

council-of-nicaea.d: The first ecumenical council adopts the Creed.

constantinople.d: Constantine moves the capital to Byzantium — the New Rome.

council-of-serdica.d: A church council in today's Sofia — "Serdica is my Rome", says Constantine.

aksum-christianity.d: King Ezana makes Ethiopia one of the first Christian states.

huns-arrive.d: They crush the Ostrogoths — the Migration Period begins.

adrianople-378.d: Goths kill Emperor Valens — Rome's worst defeat since Cannae.

empire-divided.d: Theodosius's sons split Rome into West and East for good.

sack-of-rome-410.d: For the first time in 800 years Rome falls to an enemy.

theodosian-walls.d: A double wall that guards Constantinople for a thousand years.

catalaunian-plains.d: Aetius and the Visigoths stop Attila in Gaul.

fall-of-western-rome.t: The end of the Western Roman Empire
fall-of-western-rome.d: Odoacer deposes the last emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
fall-of-western-rome.w: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

clovis-baptism.d: The Frankish king accepts Catholicism — the foundation of future France.

hagia-sophia.d: Justinian opens the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years.

code-of-justinian.d: Roman law is compiled — the basis of European law.

plague-of-justinian.d: The first great plague pandemic ravages the Mediterranean.

buddhism-reaches-japan.d: The Korean kingdom of Baekje sends a statue of the Buddha and sutras.

muhammad.d: The Prophet of Islam is born in Mecca.

grand-canal.d: The Sui dynasty links the Yellow River with the Yangtze.

hijra.d: Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina — year one of the Islamic calendar.

old-great-bulgaria.d: Khan Kubrat unites the Bulgars on the steppe north of the Black Sea.

yarmuk.d: The Arabs defeat the Byzantines and Syria passes to the Caliphate.

qadisiyyah.d: The Arabs break the Sasanians; Persia will soon be Muslim.

battle-of-ongal.d: Asparuh defeats Constantine IV's Byzantine army at the Danube delta.

founding-of-danube-bulgaria.d: Byzantium recognises Asparuh's state — Bulgaria is on the map.

arabs-in-spain.d: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses Gibraltar and defeats the Visigoths.

tervel-saves-constantinople.d: The Bulgars rout the Arabs beneath the city walls.

poitiers-732.d: Charles Martel halts the Arab advance into France.

talas.d: The Abbasids defeat the Tang; captured Chinese teach the Arabs to make paper.

founding-of-baghdad.d: Caliph al-Mansur's Round City — centre of the Islamic Golden Age.

lindisfarne.d: The raid on the monastery marks the start of the Viking Age.

charlemagne-crowned.d: The Pope crowns him emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.

angkor-founded.d: Jayavarman II founds the Khmer Empire.

battle-of-varbitsa.t: The Battle of the Varbitsa Pass
battle-of-varbitsa.d: Khan Krum destroys Nikephoros I's army and makes a cup of the emperor's skull.

house-of-wisdom.d: Baghdad translates Greek science; al-Khwarizmi writes the algebra.

glagolitic.d: Cyril and Methodius create an alphabet for the Slavic language.

christianization-of-bulgaria.d: Prince Boris I accepts Christianity from Byzantium.

diamond-sutra.d: The oldest dated printed book — printed from wooden blocks.

disciples-in-bulgaria.t: Cyril and Methodius's disciples in Bulgaria
disciples-in-bulgaria.d: Clement, Naum and Angelarius find refuge — the Preslav and Ohrid schools.

simeon-golden-age.t: Tsar Simeon and the Golden Age
simeon-golden-age.d: The capital moves to Preslav; the Cyrillic script is created.

classic-maya-collapse.d: The lowland cities are abandoned; Tikal falls silent.

battle-of-achelous.d: Simeon routs the Byzantines — one of the largest battles of the Middle Ages.

first-bulgarian-patriarchate.d: Byzantium recognises the royal title and the patriarchate.

song-dynasty.d: Zhao Kuangyin reunites China; the age of gunpowder and printing begins.

holy-roman-empire.d: Otto I is crowned by the Pope — an empire that will last until 1806.

cairo.d: The Fatimids found their new capital next to Fustat.

leif-erikson-vinland.d: The Vikings reach North America five centuries before Columbus.

kleidion.d: Basil II destroys Tsar Samuel's army and blinds the prisoners.

end-of-first-bulgarian-empire.t: The end of the First Bulgarian Empire
end-of-first-bulgarian-empire.d: Byzantium conquers the last Bulgarian lands.

tale-of-genji.d: Murasaki Shikibu writes at the Heian court — often called the first novel.

canon-of-medicine.d: Avicenna gathers medical knowledge — a textbook in Europe until the 17th century.

bi-sheng-movable-type.d: Printing with separate clay characters — four centuries before Gutenberg.

great-schism.d: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate each other — the Church splits.

hastings.d: William the Conqueror defeats Harold — the Normans rule England.

manzikert.d: The Seljuks capture Emperor Romanos IV and open Anatolia.

university-of-bologna.d: The oldest university in Europe still operating today.

first-crusade.d: Knights from all over Western Europe set out for the Holy Land.

siege-of-jerusalem-1099.d: A bloody siege, after which the Kingdom of Jerusalem is founded.

angkor-wat.d: Suryavarman II begins the largest religious complex in the world.

cahokia-1150.d: A Mississippian city of over 10,000 people and giant mounds.

uprising-of-asen-and-peter.t: The uprising of Asen and Peter
uprising-of-asen-and-peter.d: Nobles from Tarnovo rise up — the Second Bulgarian Empire begins.

hattin.d: Saladin destroys the Crusader army and retakes Jerusalem.

kamakura-shogunate.d: Minamoto no Yoritomo takes real power — the samurai rule Japan.

sack-of-constantinople-1204.d: The Fourth Crusade turns on the Christian city.

adrianople-1205.d: Tsar Kaloyan routs the knights and captures the Latin emperor Baldwin.

genghis-khan.d: The kurultai proclaims Temujin ruler of all the Mongols.

magna-carta.d: England's barons force King John to accept that he too is under the law.

klokotnitsa.d: Ivan Asen II defeats Theodore Komnenos — Bulgaria reaches three seas.

mali-empire.d: Sundiata Keita wins at Kirina and founds Mali.

legnica-and-mohi.d: At Legnica and Mohi the Mongols rout the Poles and the Hungarians.

siege-of-baghdad-1258.d: Hulagu ends the Abbasid Caliphate; the House of Wisdom burns.

ain-jalut.d: Egypt's Mamluks stop the Mongols in Palestine.

marco-polo-sets-out.t: Marco Polo sets out for China
marco-polo-sets-out.d: He will spend 17 years at the court of Kublai Khan.

kamikaze-1274.d: A typhoon scatters the first Mongol fleet.

yuan-conquers-song.d: Kublai Khan rules all of China — the first foreign dynasty.

osman-i.d: Osman's beylik in Anatolia — the seed of the Ottoman Empire.

divine-comedy.d: Dante finishes his poem — in Italian, not Latin.

mansa-musa-hajj.d: Mali's ruler gives away so much gold in Cairo that its price falls.

tenochtitlan-founded.d: The Aztecs found their capital on an island in Lake Texcoco.

velbazhd.d: The Serbs defeat Tsar Mihail Shishman near Kyustendil.

hundred-years-war.d: England and France begin a war that will last 116 years.

black-death.d: Plague reaches Europe on ships from Caffa and kills a third of the people.

ming-dynasty.d: Zhu Yuanzhang drives the Mongols out of China.

maritsa.d: The Ottomans rout the Serbian lords — the road into the Balkans is open.

kosovo-1389.d: Serbs and allies against Murad I — both rulers fall.

fall-of-tarnovo.d: The Ottomans take the capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire.

nicopolis.d: Sigismund's crusaders are crushed; the Tsardom of Vidin falls.

ankara-1402.d: Timur captures Sultan Bayezid I — the Ottoman state barely survives.

zheng-he-voyages.d: Hundreds of Ming ships sail to India, Arabia and Africa.

grunwald.d: Poles and Lithuanians break the Teutonic Order.

agincourt.d: English longbowmen cut down the French cavalry.

forbidden-city.d: The Ming emperor moves into the new palace in Beijing.

joan-of-arc-orleans.d: The peasant girl lifts the siege and turns the Hundred Years' War.

gutenberg-press.d: Movable metal type in Mainz — books become a hundred times cheaper.

battle-of-varna.d: Władysław III dies in the last great crusade against the Ottomans.

machu-picchu-built.d: Pachacuti builds an estate high in the Andes.

fall-of-constantinople.d: Mehmed II takes the city — the end of Byzantium after a thousand years.

medici-florence.d: Lorenzo the Magnificent — Botticelli, Leonardo and the young Michelangelo.

end-of-tatar-yoke.t: The end of the Tatar yoke
end-of-tatar-yoke.d: The Great Stand on the Ugra — Moscow stops paying tribute to the Horde.
end-of-tatar-yoke.w: Great Stand on the Ugra River

fall-of-granada.d: The Catholic Monarchs complete the Reconquista.

columbus-reaches-america.d: Three ships land in the Bahamas — the world is never the same again.

vasco-da-gama-india.d: The sea route around Africa to Calicut is opened.

mona-lisa.d: Leonardo da Vinci begins the portrait in Florence.

sistine-chapel.d: Michelangelo spends four years painting the ceiling.

luthers-theses.d: 95 theses against indulgences in Wittenberg — the Reformation begins.

ottomans-conquer-egypt.d: Selim I ends the Mamluks and takes the caliphate.

magellan-sets-out.d: Of five ships, one comes back — the first circumnavigation.

fall-of-tenochtitlan.d: Cortés and the Tlaxcalans take the Aztec capital.

mohacs.d: Suleiman the Magnificent crushes the Hungarians; King Louis II dies.

panipat-1526.d: Babur defeats the Delhi Sultanate and founds the Mughal Empire.

first-siege-of-vienna.d: Suleiman reaches the walls, but winter turns him back.

pizarro-atahualpa.d: At Cajamarca, 168 Spaniards seize the Inca ruler.

copernicus.d: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres — the Sun at the centre.

potosi.d: Bolivian silver will flood Europe and China.

lepanto.d: The Holy League destroys the Ottoman fleet — the last great battle of galleys.

spanish-armada.d: The Spanish fleet is broken by the English and by storms.

imjin-war.d: Hideyoshi invades Korea; Admiral Yi Sun-sin stops him with turtle ships.

first-tarnovo-uprising.d: An attempt at liberation with help from Wallachia and the Habsburgs.

sekigahara.d: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins and unites Japan for 250 years.

dutch-east-india-company.d: The first joint-stock company with shares traded on an exchange.

jamestown.d: The first permanent English colony in America.

galileo-telescope.d: He sees the moons of Jupiter and the phases of Venus.

thirty-years-war.d: The Defenestration of Prague ignites Europe's bloodiest war so far.

mayflower.d: The Pilgrims land at Plymouth, Massachusetts.

taj-mahal.d: Shah Jahan builds a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

manchus-take-beijing.d: The Ming fall; the Qing will rule until 1912.

peace-of-westphalia.d: The peace from which the idea of the sovereign state comes.

execution-of-charles-i.d: Parliament condemns the king; England is a republic for 11 years.

second-siege-of-vienna.d: Jan Sobieski strikes the Ottomans — the start of their retreat from Europe.

newtons-principia.d: The laws of motion and of gravity.

chiprovtsi-uprising.d: The Catholics of north-western Bulgaria rise up; Chiprovtsi is burned.

saint-petersburg.d: Peter I founds a new capital on the marshes of the Neva.

poltava.d: Peter I defeats Charles XII — Russia becomes a great power.

newcomen-engine.d: A pump for water in the mines — the first working steam engine.

plassey.d: Robert Clive defeats the Nawab of Bengal — Britain takes India.

slavo-bulgarian-history.d: Paisius of Hilendar writes his history on Mount Athos — the Bulgarian National Revival begins.

watt-engine.d: The separate condenser makes it powerful enough for factories.

cook-in-australia.d: James Cook maps the east coast and anchors in Botany Bay.

declaration-of-independence.d: Thirteen American colonies break away from Britain.

yorktown.d: The British surrender — American independence is a fact.

storming-of-the-bastille.d: Parisians storm the prison — the French Revolution breaks out.

haitian-revolution.d: The enslaved rise up; Haiti will be the first state founded by former slaves.

napoleon-in-egypt.d: The Battle of the Pyramids — and the scholars who find the Rosetta Stone.
napoleon-in-egypt.w: French invasion of Egypt and Syria

napoleon-emperor.d: He places the crown on his own head in Notre-Dame.

trafalgar.d: Nelson destroys the Franco-Spanish fleet and is killed.

austerlitz.d: The Battle of the Three Emperors — Napoleon's masterpiece.

napoleon-in-moscow.d: Borodino, Moscow in flames and a ruinous retreat.

tambora.d: The most powerful eruption in recorded history — then the "year without a summer".

greek-war-of-independence.d: Greece rises against the Ottoman Empire.

ayacucho.d: Sucre defeats the Spanish — South America is free.

aprilov-high-school.d: The first secular Bulgarian school, in Gabrovo.

opium-war.d: Britain goes to war with China over the right to sell opium.

the-telegraph.d: Morse sends "What hath God wrought" from Washington to Baltimore.

revolutions-of-1848.d: Revolutions in Paris, Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan.

perrys-black-ships.d: American warships force Japan to open up.

crimean-war.d: Britain, France and the Ottoman Empire against Russia; Florence Nightingale.

origin-of-species.d: Darwin publishes the theory of natural selection.

american-civil-war.d: North against South — for the Union and over slavery.

gettysburg.d: The turning point of the war, and Lincoln's address.

meiji-restoration.d: The emperor regains power and Japan modernises within a generation.

suez-canal.d: The Mediterranean and the Red Sea are joined.

bulgarian-exarchate.d: The Sultan recognises an independent Bulgarian church.

german-unification.d: Wilhelm I is proclaimed emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.

levski-hanged.d: The Apostle of Freedom is executed in Sofia.

april-uprising.d: The uprising is drowned in blood, but the world learns about Bulgaria.

botev-band.d: Hristo Botev seizes the steamer Radetzky and dies in the Vratsa mountains.

the-telephone.d: Alexander Graham Bell patents his device.

shipka-pass.d: Russian soldiers and Bulgarian volunteers hold the pass.

siege-of-plevna.d: For five months Osman Pasha holds the town against Russians and Romanians.

liberation-of-bulgaria.d: The Treaty of San Stefano — Bulgaria is back on the map.

congress-of-berlin.d: The Great Powers tear San Stefano Bulgaria into three.

tarnovo-constitution.d: One of the most democratic constitutions of its day.

edisons-light-bulb.d: A carbon filament that glows for 13 hours.

krakatoa.d: The blast is heard 4,800 km away; the tsunami kills tens of thousands.

berlin-conference.d: The European powers carve up Africa at a table.

bulgarian-unification.d: Eastern Rumelia joins the Principality of Bulgaria.

slivnitsa.d: The Bulgarian army throws back the Serbian attack.

benz-motorwagen.d: A three-wheeler with an internal combustion engine.

eiffel-tower.d: Built for the World's Fair on the centenary of the Revolution.

first-modern-olympics.d: Athens revives the games after 1,500 years.

adwa.d: Ethiopia defeats Italy and keeps its independence.

ilinden-preobrazhenie.d: Macedonia and the Adrianople region rise against Ottoman rule.

first-flight.d: The Wright brothers fly for 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk.

tsushima.d: Japan destroys the Russian fleet — the first victory of an Asian power over a European one.

relativity.d: Einstein publishes four papers that change physics.

bulgarian-independence.d: Ferdinand proclaims the Tsardom of Bulgaria in Tarnovo.

xinhai-revolution.d: The last emperor of China falls.

amundsen-south-pole.d: The Norwegians beat Scott by five weeks.

titanic.d: The "unsinkable" ship sinks on her maiden voyage.

first-balkan-war.d: Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece and Montenegro push the Ottomans out of Europe.

siege-of-adrianople-1913.d: The Bulgarian army storms the "impregnable" fortress.

second-balkan-war.d: The former allies turn on Bulgaria — the first national catastrophe.

sarajevo.d: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparks the First World War.

marne.d: The German advance is stopped before Paris; trench warfare begins.

panama-canal.d: The Atlantic and the Pacific are joined.

gallipoli.d: The Entente tries to force the Dardanelles and fails.

armenian-genocide.d: Hundreds of thousands of Armenians are killed and driven out of Anatolia.

verdun-somme.d: Two battles with over a million and a half casualties for a few kilometres.

tutrakan.d: The Bulgarian army takes the Danube fortress in five days.

october-revolution.d: Lenin's Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd.

doiran-1918.d: The Bulgarians hold their positions while the front collapses at Dobro Pole.

spanish-flu.d: A pandemic that killed more people than the war.

treaty-of-versailles.d: The peace that sowed the next war.

treaty-of-neuilly.d: Bulgaria loses the Western Outlands and its access to the Aegean.

ussr-founded.d: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia unite.

republic-of-turkey.d: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk founds modern Turkey.

penicillin.d: Fleming notices a mould that kills bacteria.

great-depression.d: The Wall Street Crash plunges the world into crisis.

salt-march.d: Gandhi and his followers walk 390 km against the British salt tax.

nanjing-massacre.d: The Japanese army kills tens of thousands of civilians.

battle-of-britain.d: The Luftwaffe fails to win the skies over England.

treaty-of-craiova.d: Southern Dobruja returns to Bulgaria without a war.

pearl-harbor.d: Japan strikes the US fleet; the United States enters the war.

stalingrad.d: The bloodiest battle in history — the turning point of the war.

midway.d: The US sinks four Japanese aircraft carriers.

rescue-of-bulgarian-jews.t: The rescue of the Bulgarian Jews
rescue-of-bulgarian-jews.d: MPs, the Church and citizens stop the deportation of 48,000 people.

hiroshima-nagasaki.d: The atomic bombs end the war with Japan.
hiroshima-nagasaki.w: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

united-nations.d: 51 countries sign the Charter in San Francisco.

indian-independence.d: British India is partitioned into India and Pakistan.

israel.d: The state is proclaimed and the first Arab–Israeli war begins.

berlin-blockade.d: The West supplies Berlin by air for a whole year.

korean-war.d: The first hot war of the Cold War.

everest.d: Hillary and Tenzing Norgay stand on the summit.

double-helix.d: Watson and Crick describe the structure of DNA.

hungarian-revolution.d: Soviet tanks crush the uprising in Budapest.

sputnik.d: The first artificial satellite — the Space Age begins.

berlin-wall.d: Overnight the city is cut in two.

cuban-missile-crisis.d: Thirteen days on the brink of nuclear war.

vietnam-war.d: The US sends in ground troops.

moon-landing.d: Armstrong and Aldrin step onto the Sea of Tranquility.

arpanet.d: The first message between two computers — "LO", before it crashed.

iranian-revolution.d: The Shah flees; Khomeini founds an Islamic republic.

chernobyl.d: The worst nuclear accident in history.

shipka-mission.d: The second Bulgarian cosmonaut works aboard the Mir station.

fall-of-berlin-wall.t: The fall of the Berlin Wall
fall-of-berlin-wall.d: The Cold War ends in the squares of Eastern Europe.

november-10-1989.d: Todor Zhivkov is ousted — Bulgaria heads for democracy.

tiananmen.d: The army crushes the protests in Beijing.

world-wide-web.d: Tim Berners-Lee puts the first website online at CERN.

mandela-elected.d: South Africa's first free elections; apartheid ends.

rwandan-genocide.d: In a hundred days about 800,000 people are killed.

september-11.d: The attacks in New York and Washington.

indian-ocean-tsunami.d: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake kills over 220,000 people.

bulgaria-in-nato.d: Seven Eastern European countries join the alliance.

bulgaria-in-eu.d: On 1 January Bulgaria and Romania become members of the European Union.

smartphone.d: Apple unveils the iPhone; the internet moves into your pocket.

financial-crisis-2008.d: The collapse of Lehman Brothers shakes the world.

arab-spring.d: Protests topple regimes in Tunisia, Egypt and Libya.

fukushima.d: The tsunami wrecks the nuclear power plant.

covid-19.d: A pandemic that stops the world.

russian-invasion-of-ukraine.d: The largest war in Europe since 1945.

bulgaria-eurozone.d: Bulgaria is cleared to adopt the euro from 1 January 2026.

potato-andes.d: Around Lake Titicaca the potato is domesticated — one day it will feed Europe.

sahara-dries.d: The Green Sahara of lakes and giraffes becomes desert; people move to the Nile.

bantu-move-south.d: Farmers from today's Cameroon begin a migration across Africa that lasts millennia.

harappan-decline.d: The rivers shift and the cities of the Indus valley empty.

rigveda.d: The oldest hymns of Hinduism are composed and passed down by heart.

lapita-pacific.t: The Lapita sail into the Pacific
lapita-pacific.d: Seafarers from the Bismarck Archipelago reach Vanuatu, Fiji and Tonga.

san-lorenzo.d: The first great centre in Mesoamerica — with the colossal stone heads.

samoa-tonga.d: The Lapita reach Western Polynesia — Polynesian culture is born here.

kingdom-of-kush.d: The Nubians of Napata break free from Egypt.

kushites-rule-egypt.d: Piye of Napata founds the 25th Dynasty — the "Black Pharaohs".

upanishads.d: Indian sages seek the unity of the self and the world.

mahavira-jainism.d: The teaching of non-violence towards every living being.

nok-iron.d: In today's Nigeria — terracotta heads and the first ironsmiths south of the Sahara.

monte-alban.d: The Zapotecs build a capital on a levelled hilltop in the Oaxaca valley.

meroitic-script.d: The Kushites create their own alphabet — still not fully deciphered.

buddhism-sri-lanka.d: Ashoka's son Mahinda converts the king of Anuradhapura.

nazca-lines.t: The Nazca draw on the desert
nazca-lines.d: Giant lines and figures that can only be seen whole from above.

sanchi-stupa.d: One of the oldest stone Buddhist monuments in India.

teotihuacan-rises.d: The city the Aztecs would call "the place where the gods were born" begins.

kushan-empire.d: The Yuezhi build an empire from the Aral Sea to the Ganges — where India, Persia and Greece meet.

aksum-trade.t: Aksum trades with Rome and India
aksum-trade.d: The Ethiopian kingdom strikes its own coins and controls the Red Sea.

pyramid-of-the-sun.d: One of the largest pyramids in the world rises at Teotihuacan.

maya-glyphs.d: The Classic period: city-states with a calendar, a zero and writing.

kofun-yamato.d: Giant keyhole-shaped burial mounds — the birth of the Japanese state.

ghana-empire.d: Wagadu, "the land of gold", controls the trade across the Sahara.

polynesians-hawaii.d: In double canoes they reach the most isolated archipelago on Earth.

nalanda.d: The Buddhist university in Bihar — with thousands of students from all over Asia.

zero-in-india.d: A positional number system with zero — the Arabs will bring it to Europe.

caracol-defeats-tikal.d: The war between Maya cities begins Tikal's 130-year "hiatus".

pakal-the-great.d: 68 years on the throne and a tomb with the famous sarcophagus.

tibetan-empire.d: Songtsen Gampo unites Tibet and introduces writing.

taika-reform.d: Japan copies the Chinese state: laws, taxes, a capital.

silla-unifies-korea.d: With Tang help Silla defeats Baekje and Goguryeo.

srivijaya.d: A maritime empire from Sumatra controls the Strait of Malacca.

tiwanaku-wari.d: The two Andean empires that came before the Incas.

borobudur.d: The largest Buddhist temple in the world — on the island of Java.

swahili-cities.d: Kilwa, Mombasa, Zanzibar — ports between Africa, Arabia and India.

chichen-itza.d: The new Maya centre in Yucatán with the pyramid of Kukulcán.

igbo-ukwu.d: Exquisite bronzes in today's Nigeria — long before Benin.

toltecs-tula.d: The warlike Toltecs become a legend for everyone after them in Mexico.

ile-ife.d: The sacred city of the Yoruba and its naturalistic bronze heads.

rajendra-chola-raid.d: The Tamil fleet attacks Srivijaya — India at sea.

cahokia-1050.d: The largest city north of Mexico before Columbus.

almoravids-ghana.d: Berber warriors weaken "the land of gold".

easter-island.d: Polynesians settle Rapa Nui and begin raising the moai.

lalibela.d: Ethiopian churches carved whole out of the rock.

great-zimbabwe.d: Stone walls without mortar — the centre of the gold trade.

delhi-sultanate.d: Qutb ud-Din Aibak founds the first great Muslim state in India.

qutb-minar.d: A 73-metre minaret of red stone in Delhi.

maori-new-zealand.d: Polynesians settle the last large unpeopled land.

solomonic-dynasty.d: Yekuno Amlak claims descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

great-drought-southwest.t: The Great Drought in the Southwest
great-drought-southwest.d: The Ancestral Puebloans leave their cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde.

second-kamikaze.d: A typhoon sinks Kublai Khan's huge fleet off Japan.

vijayanagara.d: A Hindu empire in South India whose capital Hampi is among the largest cities on Earth.

ayutthaya-kingdom.d: A Siamese kingdom that will rule Thailand for four centuries.

joseon-dynasty.d: Korea under a new dynasty that will last until 1910.

malacca-sultanate.d: A port sultanate at the crossroads of the spice trade.

angkor-abandoned.d: The Siamese sack the Khmer capital.

pachacuti-inca-empire.d: Cusco becomes the centre of Tawantinsuyu — "the four parts of the world".

hangul.d: King Sejong creates a simple script for all the people.

songhai.d: Sonni Ali takes Timbuktu — the largest empire in African history.

templo-mayor.d: The Aztecs consecrate the temple with thousands of sacrifices.

cabral-brazil.d: The Portuguese stray from the route to India and reach South America.

portuguese-goa.d: Afonso de Albuquerque makes Goa the capital of Portuguese India.

fall-of-malacca.d: The Portuguese seize the key to the spice trade.

chaldiran.d: Ottoman cannon crush the Persian Safavids.

afonso-kongo-letters.t: Nzinga Mbemba writes to the King of Portugal
afonso-kongo-letters.d: The ruler of Kongo protests against the slave trade.

manila-founded.d: Spain makes Manila the capital of the Philippines — the hub of the first global trade.

tokugawa-shogunate.d: Edo becomes the capital; 250 years of peace and a closed Japan.

europeans-australia.d: The Dutchman Willem Janszoon lands in Queensland.

nzinga-mbandi.d: The queen of Ndongo and Matamba fights the Portuguese for decades.

tasman.d: Abel Tasman sights Tasmania and New Zealand.

cape-colony.d: The Dutch company founds a station at the Cape of Good Hope.

koxinga.d: The pirate and general Zheng Chenggong takes Taiwan.

shivaji.d: Crowned emperor of the Marathas — the beginning of the end for the Mughals.

ashanti-empire.d: Osei Tutu and the Golden Stool unite the Ashanti.

nader-shah.d: The Persian conqueror will sack Delhi and carry off the Peacock Throne.

third-panipat.d: The Afghans rout the Marathas in one of the bloodiest battles of the century.

death-of-cook.d: James Cook is killed in Hawaii.

first-fleet.d: Britain founds a penal colony in Australia.

independent-haiti.d: The first state born of a successful slave revolt.

mexican-independence.d: The priest Hidalgo rings the bell at Dolores.

shaka-zulu.d: Shaka turns the Zulu into a military power that shakes southern Africa.

treaty-of-waitangi.d: Māori chiefs and Britain — the beginning of modern New Zealand.

taiping-rebellion.d: The bloodiest civil war of the 19th century — 20 million dead.

indian-rebellion-1857.d: The sepoys rise up; afterwards India passes to the British Crown.

canadian-confederation.d: Britain's North American colonies unite in a dominion.

isandlwana.d: The Zulu destroy a British army.

boer-war.d: Britain fights the Boer republics; concentration camps for civilians.

australian-federation.d: The six colonies become one country.

mexican-revolution.d: Zapata and Pancho Villa — a decade of civil war.

ghana-independence.t: Ghana — the first to be free
ghana-independence.d: Kwame Nkrumah leads the first colony south of the Sahara to independence.

cultural-revolution.d: Mao unleashes the Red Guards — a decade of chaos in China.

bangladesh.d: East Pakistan wins independence after a bloody war.

khmer-rouge.d: Pol Pot empties Cambodia's cities; about two million die.

deng-reforms.d: China opens its economy — the start of the fastest growth in history.

otrar-bukhara.d: After his envoys are killed at Otrar, Genghis Khan destroys the Khwarazmian Empire; Bukhara and Samarkand fall.
otrar-bukhara.w: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire

timur-samarkand.d: Timur makes himself master of Central Asia and fills Samarkand with the craftsmen of the cities he takes.

timur-delhi.d: Timur's army takes Delhi and plunders it for days; the Delhi Sultanate never recovers its strength.

ulugh-beg-observatory.d: Timur's grandson builds a great observatory at Samarkand; his star catalogue is the best since Ptolemy.

nader-delhi.d: The Persian ruler defeats the Mughals at Karnal and carries the Peacock Throne off to Iran.
nader-delhi.w: Nader Shah's invasion of the Mughal Empire

sikh-empire.d: The Sikh leader takes Lahore and builds an empire across the Punjab.

amritsar-massacre.d: British troops fire on an unarmed crowd in the Jallianwala Bagh; the massacre turns India against British rule.

gandhi-killed.d: Five months after independence, Mahatma Gandhi is shot in Delhi on his way to prayer.

soviet-afghan-war.d: Soviet troops enter Afghanistan to prop up its communist government and leave ten years later, beaten by the mujahideen.

bhopal.d: A gas leak at a pesticide plant kills thousands in their sleep — the worst industrial disaster in history.

canton-system.d: The Qing emperor allows Western ships to trade only at Canton, through licensed Chinese merchants.

macartney.d: Britain's envoy asks the Qianlong Emperor for open trade; the emperor answers that China needs nothing from Britain.

treaty-of-nanking.d: Defeated in the Opium War, China cedes Hong Kong and opens five ports — the first of the 'unequal treaties'.

boxer-rebellion.d: The Boxers rise against foreigners and besiege the legations in Beijing until an eight-nation army takes the city.

korea-annexed.d: Korea becomes a Japanese colony for thirty-five years, until 1945.

dien-bien-phu.d: The Viet Minh besiege and take the French base; France leaves Indochina and Vietnam is split in two.

shinkansen.d: Japan opens the first high-speed railway between Tokyo and Osaka, days before the Tokyo Olympics.

fall-of-saigon.d: North Vietnamese tanks enter Saigon; the last Americans leave by helicopter and Vietnam is united.

hong-kong-handover.d: After 156 years as a British colony, Hong Kong passes to China as a special administrative region.

sokoto.d: Usman dan Fodio leads a holy war across Hausaland and founds the largest state in 19th-century West Africa.

great-trek.d: Boer settlers leave the British Cape in ox-wagons for the interior, where they found their own republics.

victoria-falls.d: David Livingstone is the first European to see the falls the local people call 'the smoke that thunders'.

congo-free-state.d: King Leopold II of Belgium takes the Congo as his own property; forced rubber labour costs millions of lives.

omdurman.d: Kitchener's machine guns destroy the Mahdist army in a morning; Sudan comes under British and Egyptian rule.

mau-mau.d: Kikuyu fighters rise against British settlers in Kenya; the brutal war leads to independence in 1963.

biafra.d: Biafra breaks away from Nigeria; the blockade and famine kill up to two million people.

south-sudan-independence.d: After decades of war and a referendum, South Sudan breaks away from Sudan — the world's newest state.

crossing-of-the-andes.d: José de San Martín takes his army over the Andes and frees Chile at Chacabuco.

boyaca.d: Simón Bolívar defeats the Spanish and enters Bogotá; Gran Colombia is born.

mexican-american-war.d: The United States takes Mexico City; Mexico loses half its territory, from Texas to California.

california-gold-rush.d: Gold at Sutter's Mill draws three hundred thousand people west; San Francisco grows from a village into a city.

lincoln-killed.d: Five days after the Confederacy surrenders, Abraham Lincoln is shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington.

lei-aurea.d: Princess Isabel signs the Golden Law; Brazil is the last country in the Americas to end slavery.

chaco-war.d: Bolivia and Paraguay fight over the dry Gran Chaco, thought to hold oil; Paraguay wins most of it.

chile-coup.d: The army bombs the presidential palace; Salvador Allende dies and Augusto Pinochet rules for seventeen years.

falklands-war.d: Argentina seizes the Falkland Islands; Britain sends a fleet and retakes them after ten weeks.

kingdom-of-hawaii.d: Kamehameha the Great brings all the islands of Hawaii under one crown.

australian-gold-rush.d: Gold near Bathurst and then at Ballarat brings a flood of migrants; Australia's population triples in ten years.

nz-women-vote.d: New Zealand is the first country where women win the right to vote in national elections.

bikini-tests.d: The United States explodes atomic bombs over a lagoon in the Marshall Islands; the islanders are moved away for good.

sydney-opera-house.d: Jørn Utzon's sails of white tiles open on Sydney Harbour after sixteen years of building.

natufians.d: The first settled hunter-gatherers of the Levant — living in villages before farming.

jomon.d: Hunters and fishers in Japan with the oldest pottery in the world.

anatolian-neolithic.d: Çatalhöyük and its neighbours — the first large farming towns.

yangshao.d: Neolithic farmers on the Yellow River with painted pottery.

karanovo-hamangia.d: Neolithic and Copper Age tell settlements in Thrace and Dobruja.

varna-culture.d: The makers of the oldest worked gold in the world.

cucuteni-trypillia.d: Huge settlements of up to 15,000 people between the Carpathians and the Dnieper.

ubaid.d: The first temples and irrigation canals in southern Mesopotamia.

sumer.d: Ur, Uruk, Lagash — the first cities, writing and laws.

megalithic-europe.d: Stonehenge, Carnac, Newgrange — stone monuments along the Atlantic coast.

yamnaya.d: Steppe herders with wagons — probably the first Indo-Europeans.

indus-valley.d: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa: brick cities, drains, an undeciphered script.

norte-chico.d: Caral and thirty more towns on the Peruvian coast — the oldest civilization in the Americas.

elam.d: A kingdom in today's south-western Iran, Mesopotamia's eternal rival.

minoans.d: The palaces of Crete, sea trade and the dolphin frescoes.

bell-beaker.d: A shared burial fashion from Portugal to Hungary.

shang.d: The first Chinese dynasty with written records — oracle bones and bronze.

mycenaean-greece.d: The kings of Agamemnon's age and Linear B.

hittites.d: A kingdom in Anatolia, among the first to forge iron.

olmecs.d: The colossal stone heads — the "mother culture" of Mesoamerica.

lapita.d: The seafarers who settled the Pacific from New Guinea to Samoa.

thracians.d: By Herodotus the most numerous people after the Indians — in the lands of today's Bulgaria.

phoenicians.d: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos — seafarers, purple traders, inventors of the alphabet.

urnfield.d: Cremation and urns across Central Europe in the Late Bronze Age.

chavin.d: The Andean religious centre whose style united Peru.

etruscans.d: The people who taught the Romans cities, gladiators and divination.

nok.d: Terracotta heads and early iron in today's Nigeria.

scythians.d: Mounted nomads of the steppe, famous for their gold and for shooting backwards.

celts.d: The Celts of Hallstatt and La Tène — from Spain to Galatia.

sao.d: A civilization around Lake Chad, known from bronzes and legends.

sarmatians.d: Iranian nomads, the Scythians' heirs on the steppe.

nazca.d: The lines in the desert that can only be seen from above.

hopewell.d: A network of mounds and trade from the Rockies to the Gulf of Mexico.

moche.d: The Temples of the Sun and the Moon and portrait pottery.

classic-maya.d: Tikal, Palenque, Copán — city-states with a calendar and writing.

slavs.d: The Slavic tribes spread from the Dnieper to the Elbe and the Balkans.

avars.d: The steppe khaganate in Pannonia that terrorised Byzantium and the Franks.

vikings.d: Scandinavians who sailed from Newfoundland to Baghdad.

mississippian.d: Cahokia and hundreds of earthen mounds along the Mississippi.

ancestral-puebloans.d: Cliff villages of Chaco Canyon and Mesa Verde.

polynesians.d: The last great wave — Hawaii, Easter Island and New Zealand.

great-zimbabwe-culture.d: Stone walls without mortar and a gold trade reaching China.

swahili.d: Port cities from Mogadishu to Sofala — Africa, Arabia and India in one.

thule.d: The ancestors of the Inuit, who crossed the Arctic in two centuries.

silk-road.d: A network of caravan routes between China and the Mediterranean — silk going west, silver and horses going east, ideas both ways.

spice-route.d: Pepper, cinnamon and cloves on the monsoon winds from Indonesia via India to Egypt.

amber-road.d: Baltic amber travels to Aquileia, and Roman gold travels north.

incense-route.d: Camel caravans with frankincense and myrrh from Yemen to Gaza.

trans-saharan-west.d: Gold from Mali for salt from Taghaza — the wealth of Ghana, Mali and Songhai.

trans-saharan-east.d: The eastern caravan road across the Sahara.

via-militaris.d: The Roman road Singidunum – Naissus – Serdica – Philippopolis – Constantinople; later the Constantinople Road.

via-egnatia.d: The road from the Adriatic to Byzantium through Ohrid and Thessaloniki.

varangians-to-greeks.n: From the Varangians to the Greeks
varangians-to-greeks.d: Vikings down the rivers of Rus' to Constantinople — furs and slaves for silver and silk.
varangians-to-greeks.w: Trade route from the Varangians to the Greeks

hanseatic-league.d: The league of trading towns from London to Novgorod.

atlantic-slave-trade.d: Some 12 million Africans carried off to the Americas in inhuman conditions.

manila-galleons.d: Once a year a Spanish galleon carries American silver to Manila and Chinese silk to Acapulco.

settling-the-pacific.d: Austronesians set out from Taiwan and reach Easter Island by canoe.

maori-voyage.d: The last large land to be settled by humans.

bantu-expansion.d: Farmers and ironsmiths spread from Cameroon to the south and east.

asparuh-danube.d: After Old Great Bulgaria breaks up, Asparuh leads his Bulgars to the Danube delta.

alexander-campaign.d: From Macedon to the Indus and back to Babylon in eleven years, without losing a battle.

hannibal-alps.d: From New Carthage over the Pyrenees and the Alps to Cannae.

first-crusade-route.d: From the Rhine through the Balkans and Anatolia to Jerusalem.

mongols-in-europe.d: Batu and Subutai ride through Rus', Poland and Hungary and return through Bulgaria.

marco-polo-route.d: Through Persia, the Pamirs and the Gobi to the court of Kublai Khan.

zheng-he-last-voyage.d: The seventh voyage of the Ming fleet — to Hormuz, Arabia and Africa.

columbus-route.d: Three ships, 33 days without land — and a new world.

vasco-da-gama-route.d: Around Africa to India — the sea route of the spices becomes Portuguese.

magellan-elcano.d: Five ships and 270 men set out; one ship and 18 men return. Magellan dies at Mactan.

lewis-and-clark.d: The expedition that crossed North America to the Pacific.

napoleon-russia.d: 600,000 go in; fewer than 100,000 come out.

royal-road.d: From Sardis to Susa: royal couriers changed horses at stations a day's ride apart and covered it in about a week.

grand-trunk-road.d: One of Asia's oldest roads, from Bengal to Kabul; rebuilt by Sher Shah Suri, it is still in use.

tea-horse-road.d: Mule caravans carry bricks of Yunnan tea over the mountains to Tibet and bring back Tibetan horses.

ibn-battuta.d: A young judge from Tangier sets out for Mecca and comes home twenty-nine years and some 120,000 km later, from Delhi, China and Timbuktu.

cortes.d: Some 500 Spaniards land at Veracruz, win over the Tlaxcalans and enter the Aztec capital as Moctezuma's guests.
cortes.w: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire

cook-first-voyage.d: The Endeavour watches the transit of Venus from Tahiti, then charts New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.

trail-of-tears.d: The US Army drives the Cherokee from their homeland to Indian Territory; thousands die on the way.

long-march.d: Encircled, the Red Army breaks out of Jiangxi and retreats some 10,000 km to Shaanxi; one in ten arrives. Mao becomes its leader on the way.

ovid.t: poet, died in exile on the Black Sea

wu-zetian.t: the only empress regnant of China

george-washington.t: first President of the United States

mao-zedong.t: founder of the People's Republic of China

john-atanasoff.t: inventor of the first electronic digital computer

neil-armstrong.t: the first human on the Moon

ezana.t: king of Aksum, who made it Christian

al-biruni.t: scholar of India and the stars

sejong.t: king of Korea, who gave it Hangul

sor-juana.n: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz

lakshmibai.t: rani of Jhansi, leader in the 1857 rebellion

menelik-ii.t: emperor of Ethiopia, victor of Adwa

sun-yat-sen.t: founder of the Republic of China

hillary.t: first up Everest, with Tenzing Norgay

lumumba.t: first prime minister of the Congo
